recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current FHIR core source edit is needed for FHIR-14035; any desire to annotate or republish old STU3 artifacts should be handled as a separate historical-publication decision.
issue_request: FHIR-14035 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration request to delete the Practitioner comment, "Note that a cab driver no longer fits the bill. You probably would be interested in the organization rather than the individual?" Lloyd McKenzie's Jira comment confirmed removal of that note while preserving Practitioner use for people acting in a professional capacity.
initial_application: Git commit a77b1c2819418c7e6eebaad47f57213c62769019, "GF#14035: remove cab driver comment," removed the exact note from the then-authoritative source/practitioner/practitioner-spreadsheet.xml. Later source refactoring moved Practitioner into source/practitioner/structuredefinition-Practitioner.xml and source/practitioner/practitioner-introduction.xml, and those current inputs do not contain the removed note.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists practitioner=Practitioner, confirming the source/practitioner inputs are in current build scope. Exact searches find the old phrase only in tools/history/release2 and tools/history/release3 release snapshots and in the external published STU3 profile. Later Published Practitioner issues FHIR-21242 and FHIR-27900 intentionally clarified that Practitioner has wide scope, including bus/truck-driver-style organizational roles, so the current bus-driver example is a later clarification rather than a regression of FHIR-14035.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source file was edited because the current Practitioner source already satisfies the approved request, and changing historical release snapshots would rewrite old release evidence rather than fix the current specification.

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue that intentionally added wide-scope Practitioner examples including a bus driver for a community organization.
Published/Persuasive issue that expanded the Practitioner definition to include healthcare-related services and supports the current non-clinical organizational-role wording.
